newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Diarrhoea adds to Bangladesh storm misery.
newsitem.headline: Diarrhoea adds to Bangladesh storm misery.

text.p: An outbreak of diarrhoea has inflicted further misery on people already suffering in Bangladesh after a fierce cyclone battered the country's southeastern coastal region last week.
The death toll from the cyclone has risen to 111 while 23 other people have since died from diarrhoea, officials said on Monday.
About 400 fisherman are still missing at sea.
Officials said about 5,000 people in the cyclone-hit areas contracted diarrhoea, caused by drinking polluted water or eating rotten food. But officials said the situation had not yet become alarming.

Local Red Crescent officials in Chittagong port city, which also suffered badly when the cyclone with 200 kph (125 mph) winds swept in from the Bay of Bengal, said on Sunday the "spread of the disease has been contained". Unofficial sources said the cyclone left at least 121 people dead and diarrhoea had killed more than 30 up till Sunday. They put the number of people suffering from diarrhoea at up to 30,000.

Relief and medical operations had been stepped up, officials said. The government and the Red Crescent society have jointly launched a special programme to rebuild flattened houses and build thousands of new low-cost homes for people in coastal areas, they said. Saudi Arabia and India airlifted two plane loads of relief materials to Dhaka on Sunday, and officials said more would follow.
Bangladesh did not appeal for international cyclone aid, but said it would accept voluntary offers.
